purpose: Read, edit, save and arrange Morrow documents, keep persistent bookmarks, query project state, run curated tasks and present marked reviews. Responses describe actual GUI application; asynchronous loads/saves remain pending until status confirms completion.

coordinates.positions: 1-based lines and Unicode scalar columns, including the boundary after a line's last character. CRLF cannot be split.
coordinates.annotations: end inclusive; omitted end marks the entire start line

ids: Tab and pane IDs belong to the response session (process lifetime). Pane IDs remain unique and stable across project switches; inactive pane IDs are refused, never retargeted. Bookmark IDs persist across restarts. Obtain IDs from their current list/status responses; never guess IDs.

commands.title: Implementation review
commands.note: Read the plan then inspect marked changes

editing.revision: Read/tab responses supply current revision. Required expected_revision must match exactly before any edit, replace, command or save_as. A conflict returns actual_revision and changes nothing.
editing.atomic_edits: Supply either set_text (empty string clears) or 1..256 edits. All ranges refer to the same observed text, may be supplied in any order, must not overlap or insert twice at one boundary. Validate every range and resulting size before application. Undo restores the prior text as one transaction.
editing.save_policy: Mutations change the in-memory buffer and pause autosave only for that document until a successful explicit save. Preferences stay unchanged. Unsaved text is retained for recovery. No implicit writes.
editing.insert: Ordinary Vim Insert is finished as a separate undo transaction. If finishing a counted Insert would change observed text, the request fails counted_insert_active without effects; finish it in the app and read again.
editing.new: Creates a buffer only, never writes disk. Omit path for untitled; provided absolute path must not exist.
editing.save_as: Requires a nonexistent destination; never overwrites. saving:true means pending: inspect status until saving:false and error:null. save retains current path and its external-change guard.
editing.selection: Omit range to inspect selected text/mode/history; set range with expected_revision to focus source and enter Vim Visual (empty range returns Normal). End exclusive.
editing.find: Literal case/whole-word search of the current buffer; no GUI Find query or cursor is changed. Use a returned range with selection to reveal it.
editing.replace: Literal replacement in the current buffer, all:true by default; all:false replaces the first document match. At most 10000 matches, one undo step; no write.
editing.command_behavior: Commands focus their document; undo/redo perform one step. Reload refuses dirty buffers and completes asynchronously. find_next/previous use the visible GUI Find query; explicit CLI find remains read-only. Preview requires Markdown.

layout.scope: Each project owns its tab groups, split tree, focused pane, views, navigation and scroll positions. workspace selects/restores that project; focus/tab selection/editor command selects the document's owning project. Layout actions operate only on the active workspace; inactive pane IDs and foreign-project tab IDs are refused before effects. Select the project then inspect its layout before arranging panes.
layout.document_focus: When switching projects for op:focus, prefer a pane displaying tab_id (focused matching pane first), then the focused containing group, then another containing group, otherwise add to the focused group. Omitted view preserves its saved view; explicit view changes only that pane. Layout focus selects a specific active-project pane.
layout.split: pane_id omitted uses focused pane; tab_id omitted duplicates its active document into the new pane's local tab group, with independent view/cursor/scroll but shared text and undo. Optional view chooses source/preview.
layout.assign: Adds or focuses tab_id in the target pane's local tab group; it preserves the document in other panes. Optional view chooses source/preview.
layout.resize: pane_id targets a pane's containing split; ratio must be 0.15..0.85
layout.close: Closes the pane and transfers its otherwise unrepresented tabs to a surviving pane, preserving dirty buffers. Last pane cannot be closed.
layout.close_tab: Removes tab_id from pane_id only. Shared dirty buffers remain in other panes. Refuses without effects if this is the last reference to a dirty or saving buffer. An empty split pane collapses automatically; the sole remaining pane stays open.
layout.move_tab: Moves tab_id from source_pane_id to target pane_id and focuses it; equal pane IDs reorder its local tab group. Required index is the final zero-based target position after removing any existing target reference (0..remaining target length, at most 100000); no clamping. Missing panes, missing source membership or invalid index apply no change. A cross-pane move preserves document text/undo and source navigation/view/scroll; if the target already contains that tab, its existing state is retained and reordered. An empty source split collapses. No document is closed or saved. The result returns the updated tree, ordered groups and focus; after uncertain delivery inspect layout before retrying.
layout.document_close: op:close removes each clean, non-saving document from every pane; use layout close_tab for local tab closure.
layout.observation: status.active_workspace identifies the visible project. status.layout and layout return workspace, focused pane, each pane's active tab_id and ordered local tab_ids, views, locations, orientation tree and ratios for that project only. tabs remains a page across projects with each buffer's workspace; read/edit/replace/save on inactive buffers do not change the visible project.

settings.patch: only supplied fields change; null leaves a field unchanged. Applied settings are returned, persistence is queued.
settings.smooth_scroll: false by default; input key scrolling works with either setting
settings.swap_jk: false by default. true exchanges physical j/k navigation in Normal/Visual Vim commands (including counts/operators), Explorer navigation and Markdown scrolling. Inserted text, literal f/t/r targets, arrows and page motions remain unchanged. CLI shortcut: settings swap-jk true|false.
settings.search_excludes: Persistent list of gitignore-style folder/glob rules, shared by GUI and CLI project search. Trimmed, blank entries removed, duplicates collapsed and Windows separators normalized to /. Literal leading # is supported; ! negation and malformed globs are refused before any patch field changes. Maximum 128 input rules, 1024 bytes per rule, 16 KiB total. [] removes optional filters; omitted/null preserves the current list. Changing filters cancels stale GUI search results and reruns its current query.
settings.leader_key: One printable Unicode character, including a literal space. Aliases space/comma/backslash are accepted and normalized to that character. CLI shortcut: settings leader-key space|comma|backslash|CHAR. Applied settings return the actual character.

bookmarks.list: Lists persistent session bookmarks across all projects, including closed files. limit defaults to 100 (1..500), offset to 0. Responses contain items/total/offset/has_more/next_offset; follow next_offset while has_more. Items contain ID/path/line/column/label, not document text. Use the returned IDs for remove/rename/jump.
bookmarks.toggle: Toggles the current cursor line in tab_id; omit tab_id to use the active tab. Requires a named file. Adding captures the cursor and current line context; label is optional single-line text (max 256 UTF-8 bytes). Toggling an existing bookmark removes it, so inspect list after uncertain delivery before retrying.
bookmarks.rename: Changes the label for an existing bookmark ID. An empty label clears the custom label.
bookmarks.jump: Opens/focuses the bookmarked file and reveals its location. File loading can remain pending; inspect status until the target tab is ready.
bookmarks.remove: Removes only the bookmark metadata identified by id, never file contents.
bookmarks.persistence: Bookmarks survive file closure and application restart, retain their IDs, and do not save or alter document text.

queries.diff: Bounded contiguous replacement hunk against saved buffer, not Git history; reports truncation.
queries.diagnostics: Open document's current cached language-server diagnostics; one-based Unicode range, exclusive end, clamping explicitly reported when positions are stale.
queries.search: Completes on a bounded background filesystem walk without requiring an Explorer index. Active workspace default; explicit workspace queries stay in the background. Reads saved files, excluding unsaved buffer changes. Omitted/null excludes inherits settings.search_excludes; [] removes optional exclusions; a supplied list replaces them for that request only. CLI repeated --exclude PATTERN replaces the list, --no-excludes sets []; the two flags conflict. Gitignore rules, structural VCS-directory guards, symlink guards and time/byte/result limits still apply. Results report scope:workspace_files_on_disk, actual excludes and excludes_source:settings|request. Never changes persisted settings, GUI query or active project. On invalid_search_excludes correct the saved filters or supply a valid override; on search_busy wait for running searches before retrying.
queries.git_status: Cached branch and changed files with age/loading/error; does not trigger refresh.
queries.output: Bounded task output text page with actual task status; long-line byte truncation is explicit.
queries.task: check/test/build run Cargo against the active workspace's saved files. Require Cargo.toml; never auto-save or replace a running task. stop requests cancellation; inspect output/status for completion.

batch.semantics: Ordered actions, stop_on_error:true default. Reports each completed response, stopping index and remaining count. No rollback. A per-item partial failure stops just like an error. Retry remaining actions only after inspecting state, never replay successful edits.
batch.restrictions: No nested batch, asynchronous background Search or File inside batch; run search/file separately. Read-only batches remain available during a user dialog.
batch.result_detail: Results above 128 KiB become compact effect evidence retaining tab IDs/revisions and per-item outcomes, with details_omitted:true. Retrieve omitted text/details separately. If accumulated evidence approaches the transport budget, the batch stops at the next unexecuted action with stopped_reason:result_budget and remaining count; never replay the completed prefix.

defaults.open_annotations: provided nonempty annotations replace marks for that tab; omission preserves them
defaults.review: replaces previous review marks across projects; retains all successful buffers/marks in their owning project's groups and reveals the first success's project. Use focus TAB_ID to reveal another project's item; success does not imply all files are visible together.
defaults.open: keeps existing buffer ownership; otherwise uses deepest registered containing project or creates a project for the parent directory. Reveals last success's project; clean buffers refresh asynchronously from disk
defaults.location_omitted: reveals first annotation when present; otherwise preserves document cursor
defaults.clear_marks_empty: clears all marks and review summary
defaults.relative_paths: CLI open/request use current directory; review manifest paths use manifest directory

strictness: Unknown/duplicate fields and contradictory constraints fail before effects. A user dialog blocks mutation, but read-only observations remain available.

file_actions.rename: Renames in the same parent directory without replacing an existing file/folder. Preserves open buffer contents, dirty state, cursor and attached panes; paths update after actual completion. Busy documents/jobs are refused.
file_actions.limits: At most four pending jobs; the newest 32 completed jobs are retained. IDs include the process identity and expire after app restart/eviction. status.file_jobs is bounded and may mark details_truncated; file_job returns full details.
file_actions.create_folder: Creates one new folder under an existing workspace directory without overwrite.
file_actions.completion: File returns accepted:true, applied:false, pending:true, job_id, status:pending and phase:preparing. This proves acceptance only. Poll file_job: status is pending/applied/failed, phase preparing/applying/complete, complete indicates the job ended and applied confirms the filesystem change. A successful query with status:failed is an observed failed operation. Full job evidence includes path/destination/error/updated_tabs; after ambiguous delivery inspect status.file_jobs and files rather than replaying a rename.
file_actions.scope: Registered workspaces only; canonical paths verified in a background worker. New names are single basenames, never paths. Sources that are symbolic links or Windows reparse points are refused.
